title: Start here: what the LLM Coding Workbench owns
summary: The Workbench is the coding orchestration lane between a coding challenge, semantic source objects, one model-selected action, governed source mutation, materialisation, compile/test evidence, repair and REPORT. It consumes rather than replaces Semantic Source Control/Development Desk, Intention Service, Coding Intention, API Client and the language runtime.
invariants: The Workbench does not become source authority; Development Desk/Semantic Source Store remains source authority.
The Workbench does not become language-semantics authority; Coding Intention remains an external moving dependency and is not modified from this lane unless explicitly assigned.
The model selects one allowed coding action per turn; controller-owned package/member/actor identity is not model-controlled.
Completion is evidence-gated; REPORT is not a substitute for compile/test evidence.
procedure: Inspect semantic objects through the Development Desk/tool boundary.
Let the model select exactly one exposed action.
Apply policy/Intention gating and source mutation through the existing authorities.
Materialise and verify; feed structured evidence into the next turn until completion is justified.

provenance.claim: Workbench coding lane, ownership boundaries and local SSCS path.
